ratings_why.fun: Every buy is a timing call, Waxing into the Full Moon mid-turn or selling a lit Hare is a real decision, and the cards overlap in ways the builds don't list; the swingy dark turns keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 because permanence itself is the mechanic: a visible personal clock turns every stat into a timed resource you can double, cash as gold, lend to another tribe or speed up, which no tribe today does.

verdict_why: One real rules gap (The Hare in the Moon on the New Moon change) needs a line; the rest is ready.

points.text: When the Moon turns to New, does The Hare in the Moon's +3/+3 land before or after the light goes out? It isn't a New Moon effect, so the order isn't stated, and it decides whether that gift lasts a whole cycle or vanishes.

Unlisted combo worth naming in the builds: Sister Silverpenny copying Old Wat at the Full Moon takes half her neighbours' lost light as fresh Moonlight after the reset, then changes back and keeps it, so a Hare carries light across the New Moon.
Leveret's 'biggest unit next to this' can be a Hare, which hands lost light back as fresh light for a full cycle; that relay is the tribe's nicest seating puzzle and could be called out.
Spring-Ring Jill does one plain job; a hook into Wax or lost light (say, more if played after a Wax this turn) would give the opener a decision too.

With Dew-Pond Scryers and Moon-Caller you can pass several New Moons in one turn, and Mother has no once-a-turn limit, so she banks and summons Jacks each time; a fun high roll, worth seeing in a sim before touching.

standouts.why: A plain 'When played: Wax' becomes the tribe's steering wheel: Wax into Full before buying buffs, or into New after the fight light is spent.
Copies the carry from another tribe, or Old Wat, and her ruling makes the copy timing a puzzle rather than a muddle.
Seating Cutters where the zigzag touches four Hares, under Waxwell and the Moon-Scour, is the deepest combo on the board.

weakest.why: A vanilla stat gift with a phase check; nothing to discover.
Giddy Jill is a solid buffer but only reads the Moon; it adds no new interaction.
Weak early, and once a turn it is a quiet payout rather than a choice.

flags.note: Golden Cutters under golden Waxwell triple three times; capped by the reset, but a one-fight lobby kill.
Fast Moon gives several New Moons a turn, each banking permanent stats on non-Hares while the Moon-Scour's counter climbs.
Order against the light going out on the New Moon change is not stated.
